c-ci-growth.label: Compound interest is repeated multiplication
c-ci-growth.summary: Each year the amount is multiplied by the same factor (1 + r/100). So times and powers move together.

c-si-line.label: Simple interest is a straight line
c-si-line.summary: Interest = P × r × t ÷ 100. With several loans at one rate, add P × t for each and divide once.

q-ci-multiple.label: How long to grow k times?
q-ci-multiple.summary: It triples in 6 years; how long to become 27 times?

q-ci-find.label: Principal or rate from two amounts
q-ci-find.summary: A sum becomes A₁ after n years and A₂ after n + 1 years; find the rate or the principal.

q-ci-fractional.label: Compound interest for years and months
q-ci-fractional.summary: 2 years 9 months with annual compounding: compound the whole years, simple interest on the rest.

q-si-two.label: Simple interest on two loans at one rate
q-si-two.summary: Two principals for different times, total interest known; find the rate.

formulas.text: A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ     CI = A − P
If the amount multiplies by m in t years, it multiplies by mᵏ in kt years
formulas.note: Triples in 6 years → 27 times (3³) in 18 years.

formulas.text: r = (A₃ − A₂) ÷ A₂ × 100 for two consecutive years
formulas.note: The gain in one year on the earlier amount.

formulas.text: Part of a year at the end: simple interest on the amount at the end of the whole years
formulas.note: 2 y 9 m: compound 2 years, then SI for 9/12 year on that amount.
One rate: add the P × t products before dividing.

q-ci-multiple.cue: 'It triples (or doubles) in n years. When will it become k times?'
q-ci-multiple.standard: Triples in 6 years. 27 = 3 × 3 × 3, so three tripling periods: 3 × 6 = 18 years.
q-ci-multiple.fast: Write the target as a power of the growth factor (27 = 3³) and multiply the time by the power.
q-ci-multiple.eliminate: The answer is a whole multiple of 6, so only the option that is a multiple of 6 survives (18 of 18, 19, 20, 21).
traps: Taking 27 ÷ 3 = 9 and then 9 × 6 = 54, treating growth as simple.

q-ci-find.cue: Two amounts at consecutive years (7,200 after 2 years and 8,640 after 3).
traps: Dividing by 1.2 once instead of twice.
Using the 3-year amount with 2 years of growth.

q-ci-fractional.cue: Time like 2 years 9 months, 'interest compounded annually'.
q-ci-fractional.eliminate: Two full years alone give about ₹1,997 (12,000 × 0.1664), and 9 more months add about 6% of ₹14,000 ≈ ₹840. That is just under ₹2,840, so only 2,837 fits.
traps: Using simple interest for all 2 y 9 m.

q-si-two.cue: Two loans (or investments) at the same simple-interest rate and one total interest.
q-si-two.eliminate: Even at 10%, 26,000 'rupee-years' would give ₹2,600. The actual ₹2,000 is lower, so the rate must be below 10%: only 8% fits.
traps: Dividing by total principal 10,000 instead of rupee-years (gives 20%).
Using the years separately instead of P × t.

pyqs.text: An amount triples in 6 years at compound interest. How many years will it take to become 27 times its original value?
solution: Each tripling takes 6 years, so 3 × 6 = 18 years.
pyqs.trick: The time is a multiple of 6 (three tripling periods): only 18 qualifies.

b.note: Three tripling periods of 6 years make 18 years, a multiple of 6; 19 is not.

c.note: Three tripling periods of 6 years make 18 years, a multiple of 6; 20 is not.

d.note: Three tripling periods of 6 years make 18 years, a multiple of 6; 21 is not.

pyqs.text: A sum becomes ₹7,200 in 2 years and ₹8,640 in 3 years at compound interest. Find the original principal.
solution: The third year added 8,640 − 7,200 = ₹1,440 on ₹7,200: 20% a year.

pyqs.text: Find the compound interest on ₹12,000 at 8% per annum for 2 years 9 months, with interest compounded annually.
solution: Simple interest on that for 9 months at 8%: 13,996.80 × 0.08 × 9/12 = ₹839.81.

a.note: Two full years give about ₹1,997 and the extra 9 months about ₹840, so the CI is about ₹2,837. ₹2,456 is not near it.

pyqs.text: X lent ₹6,000 to Y for 3 years and ₹4,000 to Z for 2 years, both at the same simple interest rate. In total he received ₹2,000 as interest. Find the rate per annum (nearest integer).
solution: Rate = 2,000 × 100 ÷ 26,000 ≈ 7.69%, which is 8% to the nearest whole number.
pyqs.trick: At 10% the interest would be ₹2,600, more than ₹2,000. So the rate is below 10%.

b.note: At 10% the interest on 26,000 rupee-years would be ₹2,600, more than ₹2,000.

c.note: At 12% the interest on 26,000 rupee-years would be ₹3,120, more than ₹2,000.

d.note: At 15% the interest on 26,000 rupee-years would be ₹3,900, more than ₹2,000.
